pins.name: VCC2
pins.text: alternate supply (10.8-13.2 V) when no 5 V supply is used

pins.name: 1T
pins.text: threshold control: to VCC1 for normal (hysteresis) operation, open for fail-safe

pins.name: R1
pins.text: R1: a 5 kohm resistor inside the chip from this pin to VCC1 (pin 15), in the block common to all four receivers and connected to nothing else - a spare pull-up to +5 V (TI 1974 schematic, page 4-81)

functions.formula: Y = NOT A (with hysteresis: low when A > VT+, high when A < VT-, else holds)
functions.text: Datasheet logic Y = A'. Inverting RS-232-C receiver with active pull-up output. In fail-safe mode (threshold control open) an open or zero input gives a high output.

rules: Normal operation (T pin to VCC1): output goes low when A rises above VT+ (0.8 min, 2.2 typ, 3 max V), high when A falls below VT- (-3 min, -1.1 typ, 0 max V); between, output keeps its previous level; input at 0 V keeps the previous level
Fail-safe operation (T pin open): VT+ 0.8/2.2/3 V, VT- 0.8/1.4/3 V (both above zero); open or 0 V input gives output high
Hysteresis VT+ - VT-: normal 0.8/3.3/6 V, fail-safe 0/0.8/2.2 V

electrical.notes: VCC1 4.5-5.5 V (or VCC2 10.8-13.2 V), TA 0-70 C. Input voltage range +/-15 V recommended (+/-25 V absolute). Input resistance 3-7 kohm. Open-circuit input voltage 0-2 V. VOH min 2.4 V at IOH -400 uA, VOL max 0.4 V at IOL 16 mA (these are test conditions; the recommended conditions give fan-out N = 10). VIH 3 V, VIL -3 V.

timing.conditions: VCC1 5 V, TA 25 C, N 10, CL 50 pF, RL 390 ohm
VCC1 5 V, TA 25 C, N 10, CL 50 pF, RL 390 ohm

timingLimits.text: tTLH typ 9 ns, tTHL typ 6 ns (CL 50 pF, RL 390 ohm)

unknown: Only typical delays are printed; no min or max.
IOL/IOH are taken from the VOL/VOH test conditions; the recommended conditions give fan-out N = 10 instead.
notes: ND-13.003.01 page 44 labels this part 'Line driver'. Every datasheet found (TI 1974, TI 1995, National DS75154) calls it a quadruple line receiver and no 75154 sold as a driver was found, so the manual's label is taken as a slip on that one entry (the 75150 above it is a driver). NORD-10 sheet 2A50 uses two 75154 as receivers for the modem's incoming signals. Y = NOT A agrees with the datasheet logic.
